target_customer: Tech startups (seed to Series D) hiring engineers, plus recruiting agencies joining the network
problem: Startups struggle to source tech talent and agencies hold candidates in silos; pooling candidates across agencies speeds matching.
business_model: Contingency placement fees, free to employers until a hire is made
product_category: Recruiting marketplace with AI sourcing and vetted recruiters

founders.name: April Chang
founders.background_notes: Former Head of Payments at PayPal and VP of Engineering at Eventbrite per YC.

technical_complexity.rationale: A marketplace and candidate matching layer on top of agency data; hard part was recruiter supply, not engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Supply of about 100 invite-only recruiters offers a weak network effect, but agencies could easily multi-home and competitors like Paraform copied the model.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbent talent marketplaces were later acquired or wound down; none absorbed 10by10's agency pooling model.

market_need_then: Tech hiring was tight in 2017 and startups paid high agency fees, but specific demand evidence for pooled agency candidates was not found in sources.

branding.domain_note: Uses 10by10.io; the site also writes the brand as 10x10.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct hiring pitch: Hire the best tech talent, 10x faster.

brand_strength.rationale: Numeric name written two ways (10by10 and 10x10) and no press about the brand found.

pivots.from: Marketplace pooling candidates across recruiting agencies
pivots.to: Tech hiring service combining AI sourcing with a vetted recruiter network
pivots.why: Not stated; site positioning changed over time

outcome_analysis: 10by10 is still listed Active as a small team running a recruiter network for tech startups, with testimonials from 2019 to 2021 and a claim of doubling business in 2020. No funding, exit or shutdown news was found, and the website footer is dated 2020, so current activity is unclear. It appears to have stayed small rather than failed or scaled.
notes: Site footer reads 2020 so it may be stale. The site lists Y Combinator and Elefund as backers but amounts are unknown. PitchBook lists it as formerly VC-backed (via search snippet). Pivot date is unknown. Competitor search returned no dated 2017 sources, so the list is empty. Wellfound's claim of doubling business in 2020 is self-reported.
